queries.question: Return the 5 products that need reordering (units_in_stock < reorder_level), sorted by the largest shortage first. Return exactly: product_id, product_name, units_in_stock, reorder_level.

SELECT product_id, product_name, units_in_stock, reorder_level
FROM public.products
WHERE units_in_stock < reorder_level
ORDER BY (reorder_level - units_in_stock) DESC

queries.question: For each product category, calculate total revenue after discounts as SUM(unit_price * quantity * (1 - discount)). Return all categories with category_name and total_revenue, sorted by total_revenue descending.
queries.sql_query:
SELECT c.category_name, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_revenue
FROM public.order_details od
JOIN public.products p ON od.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN public.categories c ON p.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.category_name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

queries.question: List customers with more than 10 distinct orders. Return customer_id, company_name, order_count, and total_order_value where total_order_value = SUM(unit_price * quantity) (without discount adjustment), sorted by total_order_value descending and customer_id.
queries.sql_query:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.company_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity) AS total_order_value
FROM public.customers c
JOIN public.orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.company_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) > 10
ORDER BY total_order_value DESC, c.customer_id;

queries.question: Using orders and shippers, compute late shipments per shipping company using an INNER JOIN on orders.ship_via = shippers.shipper_id. Return shipper_id, company_name, late_shipments = COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE shipped_date > required_date), and total_shipments = COUNT(*). Sort by late_shipments DESC, total_shipments DESC, shipper_id.
queries.sql_query:
SELECT s.shipper_id, s.company_name, 
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.shipped_date > o.required_date) AS late_shipments, 
       COUNT(*) AS total_shipments
FROM public.orders o
INNER JOIN public.shippers s ON o.ship_via = s.shipper_id
GROUP BY s.shipper_id, s.company_name
ORDER BY late_shipments DESC, total_shipments DESC, s.shipper_id;

queries.question: For each employee, calculate total revenue after discounts from their orders. Join employees, orders, and order_details, and return employee_id, first_name, last_name, total_revenue sorted by total_revenue descending.
queries.sql_query:
SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, 
       SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_revenue
FROM public.employees e
JOIN public.orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id
JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

queries.question: Find supplier pairs that most frequently appear together in the same order. First build DISTINCT (order_id, supplier_id) pairs from order_details joined to products; then form supplier pairs with supplier_id_1 < supplier_id_2 within each order. Join suppliers to return supplier_1 and supplier_2 as company names, plus co_order_count, sorted by co_order_count DESC, supplier_1, supplier_2, top 10.
queries.sql_query:
WITH DistinctOrderSupplier AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT od.order_id, p.supplier_id
    FROM public.order_details od
    JOIN public.products p ON od.product_id = p.product_id
),
SupplierPairs AS (
    SELECT o1.order_id, 
           LEAST(o1.supplier_id, o2.supplier_id) AS supplier_id_1,
           GREATEST(o1.supplier_id, o2.supplier_id) AS supplier_id_2
    FROM DistinctOrderSupplier o1
    JOIN DistinctOrderSupplier o2 ON o1.order_id = o2.order_id AND o1.supplier_id < o2.supplier_id
),
SupplierPairCounts AS (
    SELECT supplier_id_1, supplier_id_2, COUNT(*) AS co_order_count
    FROM SupplierPairs
    GROUP BY supplier_id_1, supplier_id_2
)
SELECT s1.company_name AS supplier_1, s2.company_name AS supplier_2, spc.co_order_count
FROM SupplierPairCounts spc
JOIN public.suppliers s1 ON spc.supplier_id_1 = s1.supplier_id
JOIN public.suppliers s2 ON spc.supplier_id_2 = s2.supplier_id
ORDER BY spc.co_order_count DESC, supplier_1, supplier_2
LIMIT 10;

queries.question: By customer country, compute average order value with a two-step aggregation: first compute each order total as SUM(unit_price * quantity * (1 - discount)), then average order_total per country. Return country and avg_order_value.
queries.sql_query:
SELECT o.ship_country AS country, AVG(order_total) AS avg_order_value
FROM (
    SELECT od.order_id, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS order_total
    FROM public.order_details od
    GROUP BY od.order_id
) AS order_totals
JOIN public.orders o ON order_totals.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY o.ship_country;

queries.question: Count distinct pending orders and their discounted total value where shipped_date IS NULL. Return pending_orders = COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) and total_value = SUM(unit_price * quantity * (1 - discount)).
queries.sql_query:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS pending_orders, SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_value
FROM public.orders o
JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
WHERE o.shipped_date IS NULL;
